name: Egri Bikavér
description: 'Bull's Blood of Eger': a spicy Hungarian red blend legally required to be a blend, wrapped in a siege legend nobody can verify.
funFact: The legend says defenders of Eger castle in 1552 drank red wine that stained their beards, convincing the Ottoman besiegers they were drinking bull's blood — the name only appears in records three centuries later.

serve.how: Serve slightly cool in a large glass; the blend's acidity and spice sharpen unpleasantly when warm. Decant a young bottle for half an hour. Modern Bikavér is far better made than its twentieth-century reputation, so judge a current bottle on its own terms rather than on the export wine of the 1980s.

composition.summary: A legally mandated blend of Kékfrankos with other varieties from the Eger region.

components.label: Grapes
components.detail: Kékfrankos as the backbone, blended with Kadarka, Merlot, Cabernet Franc and others.

components.label: Region
components.detail: Eger in northern Hungary, on volcanic rhyolite tuff soils.

components.label: Vinification
components.detail: Varieties fermented separately, then blended before ageing.

components.label: Aging
components.detail: 12–18 months in oak, traditionally Hungarian.

composition.process: Cool northern Hungarian sites on volcanic tuff give high-acid, spicy fruit, and the regulated multi-variety blend builds complexity no single grape supplies.

name: Villány
description: Hungary's warmest red region, hard against the Croatian border: ripe, structured Cabernet Franc that many argue outperforms the Loire's.
funFact: Villány growers pushed for Cabernet Franc to be recognised as their flagship under the local 'Villányi Franc' designation, an unusual case of a region staking its identity on a grape the world associates with somewhere else.

serve.how: Decant young bottles for an hour — these are structured wines with real tannin. Serve cool in a large glass. Cabernet Franc here is riper and denser than the Loire style, with the herbal note folded into dark fruit rather than sitting on top of it.

composition.summary: Warm-site Cabernet Franc and Bordeaux varieties on limestone in southern Hungary.

components.label: Grapes
components.detail: Cabernet Franc, with Merlot, Cabernet Sauvignon and Portugieser.

components.label: Region
components.detail: Villány in southern Hungary, warm and sheltered on limestone slopes.

components.label: Vinification
components.detail: Destemmed, fermented warm with extended maceration.

components.label: Aging
components.detail: 12–24 months in oak, a portion new.

composition.process: A warm southern climate on limestone ripens Cabernet Franc fully, and extended maceration with oak gives the density and structure the region is known for.

name: Goriška Brda
description: The Slovenian half of Collio, split from Italy by a border drawn through the vineyards: textured whites, some of them skin-fermented in the region's amber tradition.
funFact: The 1947 border cut the Collio hills in two, leaving identical soils and grapes on either side — the Italian side became famous first, and the Slovenian side spent decades being sold as bulk wine into it.

serve.how: Serve chilled but not cold — these are textured whites and over-chilling hides the almond and beeswax. Use a standard white glass, or a larger one for skin-contact bottles. If the wine is amber rather than pale, treat it more like a light red: cooler than room temperature, but with air.

composition.summary: Textured Friulian-style whites, some skin-fermented, on marl and sandstone hills.

components.label: Grapes
components.detail: Rebula (Ribolla Gialla), Friulano, Chardonnay and Pinot Grigio.

components.label: Region
components.detail: Goriška Brda in western Slovenia, continuous with Italy's Collio.

components.label: Vinification
components.detail: Ranges from cool stainless fermentation to extended skin contact.

components.label: Aging
components.detail: Neutral oak or large casks; skin-contact wines often see long élevage.

composition.process: Marl and sandstone hills with a Mediterranean-Alpine climate give ripe but firm whites, made either fresh in stainless or with extended skin contact in the regional amber style.

name: Dingač
description: Croatia's first protected appellation: Plavac Mali from a near-vertical south-facing slope above the Adriatic, powerful and sun-baked.
funFact: The Dingač slope was so inaccessible that grapes were carried out by donkey until a tunnel was blasted through the hillside in 1973 — and Plavac Mali was later shown by DNA testing to be a descendant of Zinfandel's ancestor.

serve.how: Serve slightly cool in a large glass and decant young bottles for an hour. These are high-alcohol, sun-concentrated wines with drying tannin, so they need food with fat. The vineyard gets sunlight three times — direct, reflected off the sea, and radiated from the rock — which is why the wines are as powerful as they are.

composition.summary: Powerful Plavac Mali from a steep, sun-reflecting coastal slope.

components.label: Grapes
components.detail: Plavac Mali.

components.label: Region
components.detail: The Dingač slope on the Pelješac peninsula, facing south over the Adriatic.

components.label: Vinification
components.detail: Warm fermentation with substantial extraction.

components.label: Aging
components.detail: 12–24 months in oak, often large neutral casks.

composition.process: Triple sun exposure on a steep coastal slope drives sugar very high, producing powerful wines whose tannin is softened by extended cask ageing.

name: Fruška Gora
description: Vineyards on a lone mountain rising from the Pannonian plain, worked since Roman times and now making crisp whites and the local Bermet aromatised wine.
funFact: Bermet, a spiced aromatised wine from these slopes, was reportedly on the Titanic's wine list — a claim Serbian producers repeat often and which nobody has firmly disproved.

serve.how: Serve well chilled in a standard white glass. The dry whites are light and high-acid and want drinking young. If you meet Bermet instead, treat it like a vermouth — it is fortified and heavily spiced, served in small measures cool, and is a completely different proposition from the table wine.

composition.summary: Crisp continental whites from a solitary mountain on the Pannonian plain.

components.label: Grapes
components.detail: Welschriesling, Riesling Italico, Sauvignon Blanc and Traminac.

components.label: Region
components.detail: Fruška Gora in Vojvodina, an isolated ridge above the Danube plain.

components.label: Vinification
components.detail: Cool stainless fermentation, fermented dry.

components.label: Aging
components.detail: Mostly unoaked; bottled young.

composition.process: A continental climate moderated by the Danube gives high-acid aromatic whites, fermented cold and bottled young to keep their freshness.

name: Dealu Mare
description: 'The Big Hill' on the Carpathian foothills: Romania's serious red district, where the indigenous Fetească Neagră gives dark plum and dried herb.
funFact: Romania has one of the largest vineyard areas in Europe, well ahead of countries with far bigger reputations — most of its production has simply never been exported.

serve.how: Serve cool in a large glass and decant young bottles briefly. Fetească Neagră sits somewhere between Merlot and Syrah in weight, with a distinctive dried-herb note. The region also makes convincing Cabernet and Merlot, so check which grape you have before pairing.

composition.summary: Indigenous and international reds on south-facing Carpathian foothills.

components.label: Grapes
components.detail: Fetească Neagră, with Cabernet Sauvignon, Merlot and Băbească Neagră.

components.label: Region
components.detail: Dealu Mare on the southern slopes of the Carpathian foothills.

components.label: Vinification
components.detail: Destemmed, fermented warm with moderate extraction.

components.label: Aging
components.detail: 12–18 months in oak, often Romanian.

composition.process: South-facing foothill slopes with a warm continental climate ripen both native and international varieties, with oak ageing rounding the naturally firm tannin.

name: Cotnari
description: Romania's historic sweet wine from the Grasă grape, once ranked beside Tokaji in European courts and made from nobly rotted grapes in Moldavia.
funFact: Cotnari was served at European courts in the fifteenth century and was said to be a favourite of Stephen the Great of Moldavia; it declined under communism and is only now being rebuilt as a fine wine.

serve.how: Serve chilled in a small glass, in modest measures. Unlike many dessert wines it is not fortified, so it is lighter in alcohol than its sweetness suggests. Aged bottles develop a deep amber colour and a nutty, oxidative note that is characteristic rather than faulty.

composition.summary: Botrytis-affected sweet wine from indigenous Moldavian varieties.

components.label: Grapes
components.detail: Grasă de Cotnari, with Tămâioasă Românească, Frâncușă and Fetească Albă.

components.label: Region
components.detail: Cotnari in Romanian Moldavia, where autumn mists encourage noble rot.

components.label: Vinification
components.detail: Late harvest with noble rot, fermented slowly and stopped with residual sugar.

components.label: Aging
components.detail: Several years in oak or bottle before release.

composition.process: Autumn humidity encourages botrytis, concentrating sugar and acid, and slow fermentation leaves substantial residual sugar without fortification.

name: Thracian Lowlands
description: Bulgaria's warm southern plain, home to the indigenous Mavrud — dense, tannic and spicy, from a country that once exported vast volumes of Cabernet.
funFact: In the 1980s Bulgaria was among the world's largest wine exporters, shipping enormous volumes of inexpensive Cabernet; the industry collapsed after 1990 and is now rebuilding around native grapes instead.

serve.how: Decant young Mavrud for an hour — it is a genuinely tannic grape and needs the air. Serve cool in a large glass. Mavrud ages well and the tannin resolves into something silkier after five to eight years, so a young bottle is not showing you the finished wine.

composition.summary: Indigenous Mavrud and Bordeaux varieties from Bulgaria's warm southern plain.

components.label: Grapes
components.detail: Mavrud, Rubin and Cabernet Sauvignon.

components.label: Region
components.detail: The Thracian Lowlands of southern Bulgaria, warm and continental.

components.label: Vinification
components.detail: Destemmed, fermented warm with long maceration for colour and tannin.

components.label: Aging
components.detail: 12–24 months in oak.

composition.process: A warm continental plain ripens the late-maturing Mavrud fully, and long maceration extracts the dense tannin that extended oak ageing then softens.

name: Negru de Purcari
description: Moldova's most famous red blend, made at Purcari since 1827 and reputedly supplied to both the Russian imperial court and the British monarchy.
funFact: Moldova has one of the highest vineyard-to-land ratios in the world and holds the Mileștii Mici cellars — over 120 miles of underground galleries, recognised as the largest wine cellar on earth.

serve.how: Decant young bottles for an hour. Serve cool in a large glass. The blend leans on the indigenous Rară Neagră alongside Cabernet and Saperavi, which gives it a spicier, more leathery profile than a straight Bordeaux blend — pair it with richer, spiced food accordingly.

composition.summary: A historic Moldovan red blend of indigenous and international varieties.

components.label: Grapes
components.detail: Cabernet Sauvignon, Saperavi and the indigenous Rară Neagră.

components.label: Region
components.detail: Purcari in south-eastern Moldova, near the Dniester and the Black Sea.

components.label: Vinification
components.detail: Varieties fermented separately and blended, with extended maceration.

components.label: Aging
components.detail: 12–24 months in oak.

composition.process: A continental climate tempered by the Black Sea ripens the blend evenly, and long maceration with oak ageing builds the leathery, spiced structure it is known for.
